defects.what: The brief asked for the `_store_key` docstring to be made true on both platforms "in as few words as it has now". "(mode 600 off Windows)" is true, but it adds two words. "(chmod 600)" would be true with the same word count. One-line fix.

The helper's docstring says the note is what "a config message ends with". The `_store_key` message continues after it with ": {reason}.", and every other message ends with a period after it, so "ends with" is slightly inaccurate. Saying "follows the path" would fix it. One-line fix.

structured_output.summary: This change does what the brief asks and matches the reference almost line for line. One helper, `_mode_note()`, returns "" when `sys.platform == "win32"` and " (mode 600)" everywhere else. All five messages use it, so the text off Windows is byte-for-byte unchanged, and the `chmod` call is untouched. The new Windows test sits beside the existing one, which still passes unchanged. It asserts the exact line without the parenthesis and fails when the helper is reverted (revert_py exit 1). Ruff and the full test suite pass, and only the two allowed files were touched. There are two small prose issues. The `_store_key` docstring is true but two words longer than the brief allowed. The helper's docstring says the note \"ends\" the message, which is not quite right for the key message. The report matches the diff and the checks. It says the reverted-helper failure was observed by the implementer and not re-run, and that nothing was checked on a real Windows machine.
